description: The one-call "what is up right now" answer. For an observer location and instant, iterate every naked-eye solar-system body (and, with include_stars, the bundled bright stars), compute altitude and azimuth, keep those above the horizon, rank them brightest-and-highest first, and attach a plain-language visibility note to each, along with its angular distance from the Sun. The whole sky is gated by the Sun's altitude into daylight / civil / nautical / astronomical twilight / dark, returned alongside the list, and each note says when daylight, civil twilight, or the Sun's glare hides or dims that body. `time` is a single evaluation instant, not a window — for "tonight" pass a time after astronomical dusk (use astronomy_get_rise_set on the sun to find it). Default elevation 0 m; use min_altitude to skip objects grazing the horizon. This server does not geocode — resolve coordinates upstream first; pass an IANA timezone for observer-local times on each body.

elevation.description: Observer elevation in meters above sea level. Default 0.

include_stars.description: Include the bundled bright stars alongside planets. Default false.

latitude.description: Observer latitude in decimal degrees, north positive.

longitude.description: Observer longitude in decimal degrees, east positive.

min_altitude.description: Minimum altitude in degrees to include a body. Default 0 (above the horizon); use e.g. 5 to require clearance.

time.description: Evaluation instant as an ISO 8601 UTC string, e.g. "2024-08-12T05:00:00Z". Defaults to now. A single instant, not a window. A value with no zone designator is read as UTC, not the local zone of the server process.

timezone.description: IANA timezone for localized output, e.g. "America/Los_Angeles". When omitted, output is UTC-only.

name: astronomy_list_visible

bodies.description: Every body (and optional star) above the minimum-altitude filter, ranked brightest-and-highest first.

items.description: A sky position above the horizon, with its rank and a plain-language visibility note.

angular_diameter_arcsec.description: Apparent angular diameter of the disc in arcseconds. Null for point-source convention bodies.

body.description: The body or star this position is for, echoed from the request.

constellation.description: The constellation the body currently falls within.

equatorial.description: Apparent equatorial coordinates, corrected for precession, nutation, parallax, and aberration.

distance_au.description: Distance from the observer to the body in astronomical units.

ra_hours.description: Right ascension in sidereal hours [0,24), equator-of-date.

horizontal.description: Refraction-corrected horizontal coordinates as seen from the observer.

above_horizon.description: True when the body is above the horizon (altitude > 0).

altitude_degrees.description: Angle above (positive) or below (negative) the horizon, refraction-corrected.

illuminated_fraction.description: Fraction of the disc illuminated, 0 to 1. Null when not applicable.

magnitude.description: Apparent visual magnitude (lower is brighter). Null for bodies where the engine cannot compute it.

phase_angle_degrees.description: Sun-body-observer phase angle in degrees. Null when not applicable (e.g. stars).

sun_elongation_degrees.description: Angular distance from the Sun in degrees [0,180], seen from Earth's center. A body within about 15° of the Sun is lost in its glare. 0 for the Sun itself.

time_local.description: The same instant in the observer-local timezone with offset, present only when a timezone was supplied.

time_utc.description: The instant of the observation in ISO 8601 UTC.

visibility_note.description: Server-computed one-line headline from real values, e.g. "Venus, mag -4.1, 12° above the WSW horizon — very bright". It states when the conditions hide a body: "daylight, not naked-eye visible" when the Sun is up, "N° from the Sun, lost in glare" within 15° of the Sun, and "civil twilight, sky still bright" in civil twilight. The Moon and a negative-magnitude Venus take no daylight or twilight caveat, being visible in a blue sky; the Sun takes none.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_time`: The `time` value is not a parseable ISO 8601 instant, or names a calendar date that does not exist (e.g. 2026-02-30). `time_out_of_range`: The requested instant is outside the engine's high-accuracy span (≈1900–2100). `invalid_timezone`: The `timezone` value is not an IANA zone this runtime knows. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

sky_condition.description: Sky condition derived from the Sun's altitude — the gate for whether faint objects are observable.

sun_altitude_degrees.description: The Sun's altitude in degrees that produced the sky condition.

total_count.description: Number of bodies returned above the minimum-altitude filter.

title: astronomy-mcp-server: list visible bodies
